newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Rules-Court overturns Williams' AFL ban.
newsitem.headline: Australian Rules-Court overturns Williams' AFL ban.

text.p: Victoria's Supreme Court on Thursday overturned a nine-week ban imposed on Carlton star Greg Williams for pushing an umpire.

Justice John Hedigan said in handing down his finding that an Australian Football League tribunal had either misunderstood or misapplied its laws when it suspended Williams for pushing umpire Andrew Coates in a round one match against Essendon.

"It has concluded that the evidence given before the tribunal was overwhelming that Williams did not consciously, deliberately or with awareness of whom he was coming into contact with, interfere with umpire Coates," Hedigan said of the court's decision.
Hedigan said Williams' attention at the time had been focused on Essendon player Sean Denham.
"The contact was slight, was inadvertent and was made without appreciation that it was an umpire involved and with no knowledge or intention to interfere with him," he said.
Williams had earlier successfully sought an injunction against the tribunal's decision allowing him to play until the Supreme Court decision was handed down.
